sentences.text: Marmornectes is an extinct genus of pliosaurid from the Middle Jurassic of Bedfordshire, United Kingdom.
This longirostrine pliosaurid possessed seven unique features and resembles Peloneustes philarchus most closely.
The generic name Marmornectes translates to "marble-swimmer," blending Latin and Greek roots.
The specific name candrewi honors Chris Andrew, who found the only known specimen and donated it to the Bedford Museum in 1998.
Hilary F. Ketchum and Roger B. J. Benson named the genus and its type species Marmornectes candrewi in 2011.
Cladistic analysis indicates that Marmornectes is basal to Peloneustes and other pliosaurids.
The animal lived during the early Callovian stage of the late Middle Jurassic, approximately 164.7 to 163.5 million years ago.
Other estimates place the time range for Marmornectes in the Callovian stage from 165.3 to 161.5 million years ago.
